newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan vegoil prices seen down on new supplies.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan vegoil prices seen down on new supplies.

text.p: Pakistani vegetable oil prices are likely to dip in the next trading week on arrival of fresh supplies from abroad and low domestic demand, dealers said on Saturday.
"The market remained depressed this week and vegoil prices fell slightly because markets remained shut for three days after violence in Karachi," dealer Mohammad Kamran said.
Dealers said rates would fall further on an increased vegoil supply from abroad.
Six ships with around 83,000 tonnes of vegoil are due this month, while 157,000 tonnes of unsold stocks are available in the market, they said.
Dealer Amir Chattha said there was selling pressure because most traders were unloading stocks before the close of fiscal 1996/97 (July-June).
"In the next fiscal year (1997/98), local vegoil production is also expected to remain high and we are expecting supplies of sunflower oil to start from early July."
Vegoil stocks rose to around 157,000 tonnes from 133,000 tonnes on June 14.
